`cmp_helper` compares `UniCase::new(a)` to `UniCase::new(b)` (filters.rs:284-300), which orders by the Unicode case-FOLDED characters. Folding is not lowercasing: 'İ' folds to 'i'+U+0307, so these two are EQUAL and the stable sort leaves them alone. Lowercasing put them the other way round.
Folding is length changing: 'ß' folds to "ss", so all three tie.
unicase iterates a three-character fold as (third, first, second), so 'ﬃ' folds to "iff" and does NOT tie with "ffi". The quirk is reproduced rather than corrected.
case_sensitive drops to the value model's own ordering.
Reversing the comparator does not reverse a tie: the sort is stable either way.
A composite key is a sequence, so it falls to the value model's ordering and not to the folding path.
